extracted.intended_audience: Managers, officers, counsel, and applicants for Small Business Investment Companies (SBICs); SBA staff and practitioners advising SBICs
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and operational requirements (Part 107) for Small Business Investment Companies: definitions, operational requirements, investment limits, conflicts rules, reporting/examination obligations, and transaction approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Venture Capital (§ 107.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'Venture Capital' was modified by eliminating reference to 'unsecured' in connection with debentures or loans otherwise qualifying as Venture Capital, and by requiring such financing to be nonamortizable during the first three years and subordinated to borrowings from other institutional lenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'institutional lenders' is defined to mean banks, insurance companies, and other concerns whose regular course of business entails making commercial and industrial loans or investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total funds available for investment (§ 107.202(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'total funds available for investment' includes 'Total Short-Term Assets' and 'Total Loans and Investments' of a Licensee as required to be set forth as items 8 and 14 of page 1 of Financial Report, SBA Form 468.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venture capital investments shall be valued on the same basis as the assets comprising Licensee's 'total funds available for investment.' Instructions for Form 468 are printed as Appendix 2 to the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition requirement removed (§ 107.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed requirement that every Licensee must have a board of directors of at least five members, 40 percent of whom must be 'independent,' was deleted from the revised regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revision omits the mandatory board-size and independence percentage requirement; other governance requirements remain (see qualified management).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified management availability (§ 107.101(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee is required to maintain 'qualified management' at the Licensee's office available to the public during regular business hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rephrases and replaces the prior formulation requiring a full-time qualified officer or general manager; focus is on availability of qualified management rather than specific officer title or full-time status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control and divestiture plan postapproval (§ 107.901(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions altered so that SBA postapproval applies to control divestiture plans; plans shall be deemed approved after the lapse of 90 days from filing with SBA unless notified in writing during that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed prior-approval requirement for control divestiture plans was changed to a postapproval regime; if Licensee supplies additional financing after assuming temporary control, Licensee must report the additional financing and resubmit its control divestiture plan for SBA review in light of changed circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Discretionary Portfolio—purchase from underwriters (§ 107.504(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees, in certain specified instances, are authorized to purchase stock of a small concern from underwriters participating in a public offering of such stock, subject to the overall limitation of Licensee's Special Discretionary Portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reinstates authority similar to former § 107.750 (Revision 3) and is expressly limited by the Special Discretionary Portfolio cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sales of portfolio securities to Associates without exemption (§ 107.1005(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sales of portfolio securities to be made to Associates of a Licensee are prohibited unless an exemption in writing is granted by SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a prerequisite to granting an exemption, the Licensee must demonstrate that the terms of the proposed sale are no less favorable to the Licensee than those obtainable elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on sales to competitors of portfolio concern (§ 107.1005(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sales of portfolio securities to be made to a competitor of the portfolio concern are prohibited unless (1) approved by any such concern not under Licensee's control or (2) prior SBA approval is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant details of all sales to competitors of the portfolio concern must be reported to SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idle funds placement flexibility (§ 107.808)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that Licensees place idle funds only up to FDIC-insured amounts (as proposed) was deleted; § 107.808 omits the phrase 'but only up to the insured amount.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reinstates continued authority under prior Revision 3 § 107.710 allowing broader placement of idle funds (e.g., deposits or CDs beyond insured amounts), subject to other regulatory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on overlapping officer/director roles (§ 107.702)
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer or director of one Licensee may not be an officer or director of another Licensee nor an officer or director of any person which directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with another Licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The added language clarifies and more precisely carries out the original intent to prevent common control and overlapping management among Licensees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversified investment policy (§ 107.101(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee must maintain a diversified investment policy and, unless specifically authorized in writing by SBA, may not have more than one-third (by dollar amount) of its portfolio invested in small concerns listed in any single Major Group of the Standard Industrial Classification Manual as of the close of each fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision recognizes that unanticipated prepayment of an outstanding investment may temporarily cause exceedance; prepayment and similar events beyond Licensee's control shall constitute an appropriate basis for determining no violation occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttable presumption of inactivity for Idle Funds (§ 107.1003)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rebuttable presumption of inactivity exists where a Licensee with at least one-fourth of its assets in Idle Funds on March 31 has not made any new financing during the past 12-month period totaling at least one-fourth of an average of the amount of its Idle Funds on such March 31 and on the immediately preceding September 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language incorporated to add flexibility and facilitate fair enforcement of the inactivity provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital impairment and early-warning (§ 107.1002)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital impairment exists whenever a Licensee's retained earnings deficit exceeds 50 percent of its paid-in capital and paid-in surplus. An 'early-warning' report must be filed when the deficit exceeds 35 percent of paid-in capital and paid-in surplus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying language states treasury stock may not be included as part of Licensee's paid-in capital and paid-in surplus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest—prohibitions and limited exceptions (§ 107.1004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees are prohibited from supplying funds to a small concern for the purpose of discharging an obligation to an Associate of the Licensee (paragraph (b)(4)) and restrictions are placed on 'joint financing' of the same concern by a Licensee and its Associates (paragraph (b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New provision clarifies that subparagraphs (b)(4) and (b)(6) shall not apply to transactions by Associates in the normal course of business involving lines of credit or short-term financing; additional language added to § 107.1004 addresses conflicts limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing fees for licensing and transfer approvals (§§ 107.102 & 107.701(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions relating to processing fees in connection with an Application for License or an application for SBA approval of a transfer-of-control transaction are incorporated into §§ 107.102 and 107.701(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal explained considerations governing adoption of fair and equitable user charges; fees are treated as user charges to cover processing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation parity for venture capital investments (§ 107.202(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Venture capital investments shall be valued on the same basis as other assets comprising the Licensee's 'total funds available for investment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent valuation basis across asset classes reported on Form 468.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, forms, and audit guidance (Appendices and §§ 107.1102–107.1104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for SBA Form 468 (Financial Report) and Form 684 (Program Evaluation Report), and SBA's Audit and Examination Guide (Revised Jan. 9, 1968) are incorporated and published as Appendices 1–3 and are referred to in §§ 107.1104, 107.1102(e), and 107.1102(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees must follow prescribed reporting formats and audit/examination procedures included in the Appendices when preparing financial and program reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and treatment of additional investment by banks (§ 107.811)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 107.811 (Additional investment by bank) is treated as part of the revision and becomes effective concurrently with certain other provisions as of January 9, 1968.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific constraints and effective-date coordination are implemented consistent with the Small Business Investment Act Amendments of 1967 (Public Law 90-104).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions and other listed regulatory sections (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation enumerates prohibited uses of funds, excess real estate investments limits for SBICs licensed prior to March 19, 1965, no Government sponsorship statements, and violations based on false filings or nonperformance (see §§ 107.1001, 107.1006, 107.1007, 107.1008).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While full text of each prohibition is in the referenced sections, the revision reaffirms and codifies these prohibitions as enforceable regulatory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretations carried forward (§§ 107.1401–107.1411)
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of existing interpretations (e.g., capital structure, agricultural enterprises, qualification of retained earnings as capital, affiliated concerns as single entity, maximum amortization, short-term loans to protect Licensee investment, financing for radio/TV stations, purchase of existing notes of portfolio concern) have been condensed into §§ 107.1401–107.1411 and are included without advance notice requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These interpretations provide additional substantive guidance and are exempt from 5 U.S.C. 553 advance notice requirements; consult specific § 107.14xx entries for details.
